Upon the father is the mothers' provision and their clothing according to what is acceptable. No person is charged with more than his capacity. No mother should be harmed through her child, and no father through his child. And upon the [father's] heir is [a duty] like that [of the father]. And if they both desire weaning through mutual consent from both of them and consultation, there is no blame upon either of them. And if you wish to have your children nursed by a substitute, there is no blame upon you as long as you give payment according to what is acceptable. And fear Allah and know that Allah is Seeing of what you do

2:234.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ يُتَوَفَّوۡنَ مِنكُمۡ وَيَذَرُونَ أَزۡوَٰجࣰ ا يَتَرَبَّصۡنَ بِأَنفُسِهِنَّ أَرۡبَعَةَ أَشۡهُرࣲ وَعَشۡرࣰ اۖ فَإِذَا بَلَغۡنَ أَجَلَهُنَّ فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيۡكُمۡ فِيمَا فَعَلۡنَ فِيٓ أَنفُسِهِنَّ بِٱلۡمَعۡرُوفِۗ وَٱللَّهُ بِمَا تَعۡمَلُونَ خَبِيرࣱ‏
2:234.en: And those who are taken in death among you and leave wives behind - they, [the wives, shall] wait four months and ten [days]. And when they have fulfilled their term, then there is no blame upon you for what they do with themselves in an acceptable manner. And Allah is [fully] Acquainted with what you do

2:235.ar: وَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيۡكُمۡ فِيمَا عَرَّضۡتُم بِهِۦ مِنۡ خِطۡبَةِ ٱلنِّسَآءِ أَوۡ أَكۡنَنتُمۡ فِيٓ أَنفُسِكُمۡۚ عَلِمَ ٱللَّهُ أَنَّكُمۡ سَتَذۡكُرُونَهُنَّ وَلَٰكِن لَّا تُوَاعِدُوهُنَّ سِرًّا إِلَّآ أَن تَقُولُواْ قَوۡلࣰ ا مَّعۡرُوفࣰ اۚ وَلَا تَعۡزِمُواْ عُقۡدَةَ ٱلنِّكَاحِ حَتَّىٰ يَبۡلُغَ ٱلۡكِتَٰبُ أَجَلَهُۥۚ وَٱعۡلَمُوٓاْ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَعۡلَمُ مَا فِيٓ أَنفُسِكُمۡ فَٱحۡذَرُوهُۚ وَٱعۡلَمُوٓاْ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورٌ حَلِيمࣱ‏
2:235.en: There is no blame upon you for that to which you [indirectly] allude concerning a proposal to women or for what you conceal within yourselves. Allah knows that you will have them in mind. But do not promise them secretly except for saying a proper saying. And do not determine to undertake a marriage contract until the decreed period reaches its end. And know that Allah knows what is within yourselves, so beware of Him. And know that Allah is Forgiving and Forbearing

2:236.ar: لَّا جُنَاحَ عَلَيۡكُمۡ إِن طَلَّقۡتُمُ ٱلنِّسَآءَ مَا لَمۡ تَمَسُّوهُنَّ أَوۡ تَفۡرِضُواْ لَهُنَّ فَرِيضَةࣰۚ وَمَتِّعُوهُنَّ عَلَى ٱلۡمُوسِعِ قَدَرُهُۥ وَعَلَى ٱلۡمُقۡتِرِ قَدَرُهُۥ مَتَٰعَۢا بِٱلۡمَعۡرُوفِۖ حَقًّا عَلَى ٱلۡمُحۡسِنِينَ
2:236.en: There is no blame upon you if you divorce women you have not touched nor specified for them an obligation. But give them [a gift of] compensation - the wealthy according to his capability and the poor according to his capability - a provision according to what is acceptable, a duty upon the doers of good

2:237.ar: وَإِن طَلَّقۡتُمُوهُنَّ مِن قَبۡلِ أَن تَمَسُّوهُنَّ وَقَدۡ فَرَضۡتُمۡ لَهُنَّ فَرِيضَةࣰ فَنِصۡفُ مَا فَرَضۡتُمۡ إِلَّآ أَن يَعۡفُونَ أَوۡ يَعۡفُوَاْ ٱلَّذِي بِيَدِهِۦ عُقۡدَةُ ٱلنِّكَاحِۚ وَأَن تَعۡفُوٓاْ أَقۡرَبُ لِلتَّقۡوَىٰۚ وَلَا تَنسَوُاْ ٱلۡفَضۡلَ بَيۡنَكُمۡۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ بِمَا تَعۡمَلُونَ بَصِيرٌ
2:237.en: And if you divorce them before you have touched them and you have already specified for them an obligation, then [give] half of what you specified - unless they forego the right or the one in whose hand is the marriage contract foregoes it. And to forego it is nearer to righteousness. And do not forget graciousness between you. Indeed Allah, of whatever you do, is Seeing

2:238.ar: حَٰفِظُواْ عَلَى ٱلصَّلَوَٰتِ وَٱلصَّلَوٰةِ ٱلۡوُسۡطَىٰ وَقُومُواْ لِلَّهِ قَٰنِتِينَ
2:238.en: Maintain with care the [obligatory] prayers and [in particular] the middle prayer and stand before Allah, devoutly obedient

2:239.ar: فَإِنۡ خِفۡتُمۡ فَرِجَالًا أَوۡ رُكۡبَانࣰ اۖ فَإِذَآ أَمِنتُمۡ فَٱذۡكُرُواْ ٱللَّهَ كَمَا عَلَّمَكُم مَّا لَمۡ تَكُونُواْ تَعۡلَمُونَ
2:239.en: And if you fear [an enemy, then pray] on foot or riding. But when you are secure, then remember Allah [in prayer], as He has taught you that which you did not [previously] know

2:240.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ يُتَوَفَّوۡنَ مِنكُمۡ وَيَذَرُونَ أَزۡوَٰجࣰ ا وَصِيَّةࣰ لِّأَزۡوَٰجِهِم مَّتَٰعًا إِلَى ٱلۡحَوۡلِ غَيۡرَ إِخۡرَاجࣲۚ فَإِنۡ خَرَجۡنَ فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيۡكُمۡ فِي مَا فَعَلۡنَ فِيٓ أَنفُسِهِنَّ مِن مَّعۡرُوفࣲۗ وَٱللَّهُ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمࣱ‏
2:240.en: And those who are taken in death among you and leave wives behind - for their wives is a bequest: maintenance for one year without turning [them] out. But if they leave [of their own accord], then there is no blame upon you for what they do with themselves in an acceptable way. And Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise

2:241.ar: وَلِلۡمُطَلَّقَٰتِ مَتَٰعُۢ بِٱلۡمَعۡرُوفِۖ حَقًّا عَلَى ٱلۡمُتَّقِينَ
2:241.en: And for divorced women is a provision according to what is acceptable - a duty upon the righteous

2:242.ar: كَذَٰلِكَ يُبَيِّنُ ٱللَّهُ لَكُمۡ ءَايَٰتِهِۦ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تَعۡقِلُونَ
2:242.en: Thus does Allah make clear to you His verses that you might use reason

2:243.ar: ۞أَلَمۡ تَرَ إِلَى ٱلَّذِينَ خَرَجُواْ مِن دِيَٰرِهِمۡ وَهُمۡ أُلُوفٌ حَذَرَ ٱلۡمَوۡتِ فَقَالَ لَهُمُ ٱللَّهُ مُوتُواْ ثُمَّ أَحۡيَٰهُمۡۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَذُو فَضۡلٍ عَلَى ٱلنَّاسِ وَلَٰكِنَّ أَكۡثَرَ ٱلنَّاسِ لَا يَشۡكُرُونَ
2:243.en: Have you not considered those who left their homes in many thousands, fearing death? Allah said to them, "Die"; then He restored them to life. And Allah is full of bounty to the people, but most of the people do not show gratitude

2:255.ar: ٱللَّهُ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ ٱلۡحَيُّ ٱلۡقَيُّومُۚ لَا تَأۡخُذُهُۥ سِنَةࣱ وَلَا نَوۡمࣱۚ لَّهُۥ مَا فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِۗ مَن ذَا ٱلَّذِي يَشۡفَعُ عِندَهُۥٓ إِلَّا بِإِذۡنِهِۦۚ يَعۡلَمُ مَا بَيۡنَ أَيۡدِيهِمۡ وَمَا خَلۡفَهُمۡۖ وَلَا يُحِيطُونَ بِشَيۡءࣲ مِّنۡ عِلۡمِهِۦٓ إِلَّا بِمَا شَآءَۚ وَسِعَ كُرۡسِيُّهُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضَۖ وَلَا يَـُٔودُهُۥ حِفۡظُهُمَاۚ وَهُوَ ٱلۡعَلِيُّ ٱلۡعَظِيمُ
2:255.en: Allah - there is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of [all] existence. Neither drowsiness overtakes Him nor sleep. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. Who is it that can intercede with Him except by His permission? He knows what is [presently] before them and what will be after them, and they encompass not a thing of His knowledge except for what He wills. His Kursi extends over the heavens and the earth, and their preservation tires Him not. And He is the Most High, the Most Great

2:256.ar: لَآ إِكۡرَاهَ فِي ٱلدِّينِۖ قَد تَّبَيَّنَ ٱلرُّشۡدُ مِنَ ٱلۡغَيِّۚ فَمَن يَكۡفُرۡ بِٱلطَّٰغُوتِ وَيُؤۡمِنۢ بِٱللَّهِ فَقَدِ ٱسۡتَمۡسَكَ بِٱلۡعُرۡوَةِ ٱلۡوُثۡقَىٰ لَا ٱنفِصَامَ لَهَاۗ وَٱللَّهُ سَمِيعٌ عَلِيمٌ
2:256.en: There shall be no compulsion in [acceptance of] the religion. The right course has become clear from the wrong. So whoever disbelieves in Taghut and believes in Allah has grasped the most trustworthy handhold with no break in it. And Allah is Hearing and Knowing

2:257.ar: ٱللَّهُ وَلِيُّ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ يُخۡرِجُهُم مِّنَ ٱلظُّلُمَٰتِ إِلَى ٱلنُّورِۖ وَٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوٓاْ أَوۡلِيَآؤُهُمُ ٱلطَّٰغُوتُ يُخۡرِجُونَهُم مِّنَ ٱلنُّورِ إِلَى ٱلظُّلُمَٰتِۗ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ أَصۡحَٰبُ ٱلنَّارِۖ هُمۡ فِيهَا خَٰلِدُونَ
2:257.en: Allah is the ally of those who believe. He brings them out from darknesses into the light. And those who disbelieve - their allies are Taghut. They take them out of the light into darknesses. Those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide eternally therein

2:258.ar: أَلَمۡ تَرَ إِلَى ٱلَّذِي حَآجَّ إِبۡرَٰهِـۧمَ فِي رَبِّهِۦٓ أَنۡ ءَاتَىٰهُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلۡمُلۡكَ إِذۡ قَالَ إِبۡرَٰهِـۧمُ رَبِّيَ ٱلَّذِي يُحۡيِۦ وَيُمِيتُ قَالَ أَنَا۠ أُحۡيِۦ وَأُمِيتُۖ قَالَ إِبۡرَٰهِـۧمُ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَأۡتِي بِٱلشَّمۡسِ مِنَ ٱلۡمَشۡرِقِ فَأۡتِ بِهَا مِنَ ٱلۡمَغۡرِبِ فَبُهِتَ ٱلَّذِي كَفَرَۗ وَٱللَّهُ لَا يَهۡدِي ٱلۡقَوۡمَ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
2:258.en: Have you not considered the one who argued with Abraham about his Lord [merely] because Allah had given him kingship? When Abraham said, "My Lord is the one who gives life and causes death," he said, "I give life and cause death." Abraham said, "Indeed, Allah brings up the sun from the east, so bring it up from the west." So the disbeliever was overwhelmed [by astonishment], and Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people

2:259.ar: أَوۡ كَٱلَّذِي مَرَّ عَلَىٰ قَرۡيَةࣲ وَهِيَ خَاوِيَةٌ عَلَىٰ عُرُوشِهَا قَالَ أَنَّىٰ يُحۡيِۦ هَٰذِهِ ٱللَّهُ بَعۡدَ مَوۡتِهَاۖ فَأَمَاتَهُ ٱللَّهُ مِاْئَةَ عَامࣲ ثُمَّ بَعَثَهُۥۖ قَالَ كَمۡ لَبِثۡتَۖ قَالَ لَبِثۡتُ يَوۡمًا أَوۡ بَعۡضَ يَوۡمࣲۖ قَالَ بَل لَّبِثۡتَ مِاْئَةَ عَامࣲ فَٱنظُرۡ إِلَىٰ طَعَامِكَ وَشَرَابِكَ لَمۡ يَتَسَنَّهۡۖ وَٱنظُرۡ إِلَىٰ حِمَارِكَ وَلِنَجۡعَلَكَ ءَايَةࣰ لِّلنَّاسِۖ وَٱنظُرۡ إِلَى ٱلۡعِظَامِ كَيۡفَ نُنشِزُهَا ثُمَّ نَكۡسُوهَا لَحۡمࣰ اۚ فَلَمَّا تَبَيَّنَ لَهُۥ قَالَ أَعۡلَمُ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ قَدِيرࣱ‏
2:259.en: Or [consider such an example] as the one who passed by a township which had fallen into ruin. He said, "How will Allah bring this to life after its death?" So Allah caused him to die for a hundred years; then He revived him. He said, "How long have you remained?" The man said, "I have remained a day or part of a day." He said, "Rather, you have remained one hundred years. Look at your food and your drink; it has not changed with time. And look at your donkey; and We will make you a sign for the people. And look at the bones [of this donkey] - how We raise them and then We cover them with flesh." And when it became clear to him, he said, "I know that Allah is over all things competent

2:260.ar: وَإِذۡ قَالَ إِبۡرَٰهِـۧمُ رَبِّ أَرِنِي كَيۡفَ تُحۡيِ ٱلۡمَوۡتَىٰۖ قَالَ أَوَلَمۡ تُؤۡمِنۖ قَالَ بَلَىٰ وَلَٰكِن لِّيَطۡمَئِنَّ قَلۡبِيۖ قَالَ فَخُذۡ أَرۡبَعَةࣰ مِّنَ ٱلطَّيۡرِ فَصُرۡهُنَّ إِلَيۡكَ ثُمَّ ٱجۡعَلۡ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ جَبَلࣲ مِّنۡهُنَّ جُزۡءࣰ ا ثُمَّ ٱدۡعُهُنَّ يَأۡتِينَكَ سَعۡيࣰ اۚ وَٱعۡلَمۡ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمࣱ‏
2:260.en: And [mention] when Abraham said, "My Lord, show me how You give life to the dead." [Allah] said, "Have you not believed?" He said, "Yes, but [I ask] only that my heart may be satisfied." [Allah] said, "Take four birds and commit them to yourself. Then [after slaughtering them] put on each hill a portion of them; then call them - they will come [flying] to you in haste. And know that Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise

2:286.ar: لَا يُكَلِّفُ ٱللَّهُ نَفۡسًا إِلَّا وُسۡعَهَاۚ لَهَا مَا كَسَبَتۡ وَعَلَيۡهَا مَا ٱكۡتَسَبَتۡۗ رَبَّنَا لَا تُؤَاخِذۡنَآ إِن نَّسِينَآ أَوۡ أَخۡطَأۡنَاۚ رَبَّنَا وَلَا تَحۡمِلۡ عَلَيۡنَآ إِصۡرࣰ ا كَمَا حَمَلۡتَهُۥ عَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبۡلِنَاۚ رَبَّنَا وَلَا تُحَمِّلۡنَا مَا لَا طَاقَةَ لَنَا بِهِۦۖ وَٱعۡفُ عَنَّا وَٱغۡفِرۡ لَنَا وَٱرۡحَمۡنَآۚ أَنتَ مَوۡلَىٰنَا فَٱنصُرۡنَا عَلَى ٱلۡقَوۡمِ ٱلۡكَٰفِرِينَ
2:286.en: Allah does not charge a soul except [with that within] its capacity. It will have [the consequence of] what [good] it has gained, and it will bear [the consequence of] what [evil] it has earned. "Our Lord, do not impose blame upon us if we have forgotten or erred. Our Lord, and lay not upon us a burden like that which You laid upon those before us. Our Lord, and burden us not with that which we have no ability to bear. And pardon us; and forgive us; and have mercy upon us. You are our protector, so give us victory over the disbelieving people

1:1.en: In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful

1:2.en: [All] praise is [due] to Allah, Lord of the worlds

1:3.en: The Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful

1:4.en: Sovereign of the Day of Recompense

1:5.en: It is You we worship and You we ask for help

1:6.en: Guide us to the straight path

1:7.ar: صِرَٰطَ ٱلَّذِينَ أَنۡعَمۡتَ عَلَيۡهِمۡ غَيۡرِ ٱلۡمَغۡضُوبِ عَلَيۡهِمۡ وَلَا ٱلضَّآلِّينَ
1:7.en: The path of those upon whom You have bestowed favor, not of those who have evoked [Your] anger or of those who are astray

2smyEpvgG_c.speaker: adnan
2smyEpvgG_c.speaker_note: title names Sh. Adnan Rajeh; short pre-Isha Ramadan surah-summary talk
2smyEpvgG_c.title: Surat Al-Baqarah Summary
2smyEpvgG_c.one_line: A compass for Surat Al-Baqarah: humanity's job as khalifah, examples who failed and succeeded, the struggles of life, and the easing closing dua.
2smyEpvgG_c.summary: He offers a short compass for reading Al-Baqarah so its length does not overwhelm. He first explains why he will not summarise Al-Fatihah: it is the key and reference for every surah and every word of revelation, too vast to compress. Al-Baqarah, the longest surah, was revealed across the Prophet's Madinan years. Its first 29 verses are an underrated introduction holding every core value, and he urges people to recite them more. Verse 30 then gives the human job description: you are a khalifah, acting on earth in Allah's name. Adam is the first holder of that role; the Children of Israel are the long example of a people chosen for it who repeatedly got it wrong; Ibrahim is the example of someone who perfected it and was made a leader. From the second juz onward the surah lays out a full system of life and the struggles that come with stewardship: tyranny, courage, oppression of the weak, family and marriage problems, money and riba, fasting, Hajj and fighting for what is right. Just as the reader feels overwhelmed, the final verses reassure that Allah burdens no soul beyond its capacity and give a dua for forgiveness, which is why the Prophet urged reciting them.

outline.heading: Opening
Why Al-Fatihah cannot be summarised
outline.gist: It is the key and the reference for every surah and every word Allah revealed to any prophet.

outline.heading: The longest surah, spanning the Madinan years
outline.gist: Most of it came early in Madinah, some near the Prophet's death, including what is reported as the last verse revealed.

outline.heading: The first 29 verses: an underrated introduction
outline.gist: Every ethic and value is gathered in them; recite them more often.

outline.heading: Verse 30: the human job description
outline.gist: Right at the start of the Quran you are told why you exist: to be a khalifah.

outline.heading: Adam, the first khalifah, and what khalifah means
outline.gist: Someone doing a job in the name of another; we care for the earth in Allah's name.

outline.heading: The Children of Israel: an example of getting it wrong
outline.gist: Chosen for the role, they made every mistake and failed to correct them.

outline.heading: Ibrahim: an example of getting it right
outline.gist: He perfected stewardship and was made a leader of people.

outline.heading: From juz two: the struggle of stewardship
outline.gist: Tyranny, courage, oppression of the weak, family, marital and financial problems all appear.

outline.heading: A full system of life
outline.gist: Fasting, Hajj, fighting for what is right, the ban on riba and family law are laid out with guidance.

outline.heading: Overwhelming at first, easy once you live with it
outline.gist: Ayat al-Kursi, no compulsion in religion and Ibrahim's arguments about resurrection come amid the struggle.

outline.heading: The ending makes it easy
outline.gist: No soul is burdened beyond capacity, and the closing dua asks Allah not to hold our forgetfulness against us.

outline.heading: Outro

33:9.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ ٱذۡكُرُواْ نِعۡمَةَ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيۡكُمۡ إِذۡ جَآءَتۡكُمۡ جُنُودࣱ فَأَرۡسَلۡنَا عَلَيۡهِمۡ رِيحࣰ ا وَجُنُودࣰ ا لَّمۡ تَرَوۡهَاۚ وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ بِمَا تَعۡمَلُونَ بَصِيرًا
33:9.en: O you who have believed, remember the favor of Allah upon you when armies came to [attack] you and We sent upon them a wind and armies [of angels] you did not see. And ever is Allah, of what you do, Seeing

33:10.ar: إِذۡ جَآءُوكُم مِّن فَوۡقِكُمۡ وَمِنۡ أَسۡفَلَ مِنكُمۡ وَإِذۡ زَاغَتِ ٱلۡأَبۡصَٰرُ وَبَلَغَتِ ٱلۡقُلُوبُ ٱلۡحَنَاجِرَ وَتَظُنُّونَ بِٱللَّهِ ٱلظُّنُونَا۠
33:10.en: [Remember] when they came at you from above you and from below you, and when eyes shifted [in fear], and hearts reached the throats and you assumed about Allah [various] assumptions

98_avq4W-KM.speaker: adnan
98_avq4W-KM.speaker_note: continuation of his weekly seerah halaqah; mentions his own time in Medina and digging with volunteers
98_avq4W-KM.title: Seerah Halaqah: Preparing for the Battle of the Trench (Part 2)
98_avq4W-KM.one_line: The Prophet consults the companions about the ten-thousand-strong Confederate army, adopts Salman al-Farsi's trench idea, and plans the five-kilometre trench.
98_avq4W-KM.summary: The sheikh describes the shock in Medina when news arrived that ten thousand fighters were marching on the city, while the Muslims could field about fifteen hundred. As always, the Prophet consulted his companions, and he notes that the Quran itself records their psychological state in Surat al-Ahzab. Various ideas were raised: retreating to a mountain, seeking help from northern kingdoms, or fleeing. Then Salman al-Farsi, a Persian and former slave who would never have dared speak in a traditional Arab gathering, felt respected enough to propose digging a trench. The sheikh dwells on the Prophet's open-mindedness in accepting a foreign, untested idea at an age when many people resist anything new, and insists that following the Prophet means being open to good ideas, since newness is no reason to reject something. He then explains Medina's geography with maps: lava fields to the east and west, the forts of the Jewish tribes to the south, leaving only the northern side open. He works through the trench's dimensions, the rubble piled on the Muslim side, the sixty groups of twenty-five each assigned their own stretch to dig and defend, and the ten-day deadline, which meant each man digging roughly the volume of a bedroom with simple tools.

outline.heading: News of ten thousand and the call to consult
outline.gist: The Prophet gathers the companions and asks their advice; they are stunned by the size of the army.

outline.heading: How the ten thousand were assembled
outline.gist: No tribe had such numbers; contingents from many tribes combined into one force.

outline.heading: The Quran's account of the Confederates
outline.gist: Surat al-Ahzab records the companions' fear and reactions more precisely than any retelling; he promises to explain the verses.

outline.heading: Options raised and the young sent home
outline.gist: Ideas include holding a mountain or seeking northern allies; the Prophet turns back boys too young to fight despite needing every man.

outline.heading: Every tribe sends a representative
outline.gist: Like the plot on the night of hijrah, every tribe joins so the blame is shared and no one can retaliate against all.

outline.heading: Salman al-Farsi: the man who would never have spoken
outline.gist: As a non-Arab and former slave, Salman would have been silenced in any other Arab gathering.

outline.heading: Salman feels respected enough to speak
outline.gist: He tells them that in Persia they dug a trench when attacked by a larger army.

outline.heading: The trench idea and the laughter
outline.gist: Some laugh, unsure if he is serious; the Prophet asks him to explain how it works.

outline.heading: The Prophet's open-mindedness
outline.gist: Unlike people who grow set in their ways with age, the Prophet in his late fifties welcomed a strange foreign idea.

outline.heading: Newness is no reason to reject an idea
outline.gist: Following the Prophet means listening to others' experience; being closed-minded in his name makes no sense.

outline.heading: The companions' doubts and simple tools
outline.gist: They were not builders and had only basic tools, yet the community adapted.

outline.heading: Medina's geography: the lava fields east and west
outline.gist: Deep black volcanic rock fields make the east and west impassable; he recalls dropping a stone into one in Medina.

outline.heading: The south sealed by the Jewish forts
outline.gist: With forts and huge gates in the south and a treaty with those tribes, only the north needed defending.

outline.heading: Measuring the trench: five kilometres long
outline.gist: Using maps he shows the northern gap and the length the trench needed to cover.

outline.heading: Why the width and depth mattered
outline.gist: It had to be too wide for horses to jump or planks to bridge, and deep enough that a fall was fatal.

outline.heading: Rubble piled on the Muslim side
outline.gist: The excavated earth formed a rampart for the defenders, so no real battle would happen inside the trench.

outline.heading: Sixty groups, each digging and defending its stretch
outline.gist: About sixty thousand cubic metres split among sixty groups of twenty-five, each told it would defend what it dug.

outline.heading: Leadership through knowledge of the land
outline.gist: Reviewing the map, he highlights how well the Prophet knew the geography and how carefully the plan was designed.

outline.heading: Mount Sal' and the northern line
outline.gist: He marks the mountain behind the trench that becomes central to the story.

outline.heading: Ten days: each man digs the volume of a room
outline.gist: With ten days before the army arrived, every man had to move about forty cubic metres of rocky ground by hand.

outline.heading: His own trench experiment begins
outline.gist: He starts telling how he once tried digging a similar section with ten high-school volunteers.

Respect people regardless of origin or social status
Plan carefully and give each person clear responsibility for their part

dTnRBFgfKUM.speaker: adnan
dTnRBFgfKUM.speaker_note: part of his seerah halaqah series; same voice and teaching style
dTnRBFgfKUM.title: Seerah Halaqah, November 3, 2018 (Part 4): Poetry and Hunger at the Trench
dTnRBFgfKUM.one_line: Digging the trench: chanted poetry that lifted morale, the Prophet's deliberate imperfection as a leader, stones tied against hunger, and Jabir's small meal.
dTnRBFgfKUM.summary: He describes the companions digging the trench while chanting verses: a prayer asking Allah to send tranquillity and keep their feet firm against those who wanted to turn them from their faith, and the Ansar's pledge to stand by the Prophet as long as they lived. Meaningful art, he says, does exactly this: it takes people who feel beaten, few and alone and makes them believe they can do the impossible, which is why the Prophet asked for poetry while building the masjid too. When the Prophet himself recited, he broke the rhythm, and he believes this was a choice. A leader who is good at everything cannot be related to; showing people what you cannot do reminds followers that leaders are human, not gods, which keeps the relationship healthy. Very few leaders have the courage to be vulnerable this way. Yet singing could not fill empty stomachs. Working long days in the heat with almost no food, the companions tied stones against their bellies to ease the hunger, and when they showed the Prophet, he revealed two stones tied to his own. The segment ends as Jabir, seeing the Prophet's hunger, goes home to find a tiny meal of barley and meat and quietly invites him, only for the Prophet to call the whole army.

outline.heading: "Send down tranquillity upon us"
outline.gist: The verses chanted while digging asked Allah for calm and firm feet against those who sought to make them abandon their faith.

outline.heading: The Ansar's chant of allegiance
outline.gist: They sang that they had pledged themselves to the Prophet as long as they lived.

outline.heading: What meaningful art does
outline.gist: Art with a message lifts people who feel weak and few, strengthening communities; the Prophet asked for poetry while building the masjid too.

outline.heading: The Prophet recites without the beat
outline.gist: When he joined in he broke the rhythm, and the companions noticed.

outline.heading: Choosing not to be good at everything
outline.gist: He believes the Prophet chose this so people could relate to him and find something he did not do well.

outline.heading: The courage to be vulnerable as a leader
outline.gist: Few leaders admit what they cannot do; reminding followers that leaders are human, not gods, keeps the relationship healthy.

outline.heading: Singing could not fill their stomachs
outline.gist: They worked long hours in the heat with barely a meal, and the Prophet himself went days without eating.

outline.heading: No weak links among the 1,500
outline.gist: The companions proved themselves strong under this hardship.

outline.heading: Stones tied against hunger
outline.gist: They tied rocks to their bellies to press the stomach and dull the hunger.

outline.heading: The Prophet's two stones
outline.gist: When they showed him their stones, he smiled and lifted his garment to show two tied to his own stomach, and Jabir saw it.

outline.heading: Jabir's tiny meal at home
outline.gist: Jabir's wife had only a little barley and a small piece of meat for a household with nine sisters.

outline.heading: Inviting the Prophet, who invites everyone
outline.gist: Jabir quietly asked the Prophet to come with one or two others, and the Prophet called the whole army; the story continues next time.

Art with a message strengthens communities

stories.point: Meaningful poetry lifts a community that feels weak and few.

stories.who: The Prophet reciting off the beat
stories.point: A leader's visible imperfection makes him relatable and keeps followers grounded.
The Prophet shared and exceeded his companions' hardship.
Generosity offered with little, and the Prophet's concern to feed everyone.

If you lead, be honest about what you cannot do.

Offer what you have, even if it seems too little.

24:16.ar: وَلَوۡلَآ إِذۡ سَمِعۡتُمُوهُ قُلۡتُم مَّا يَكُونُ لَنَآ أَن نَّتَكَلَّمَ بِهَٰذَا سُبۡحَٰنَكَ هَٰذَا بُهۡتَٰنٌ عَظِيمࣱ‏
24:16.en: And why, when you heard it, did you not say, "It is not for us to speak of this. Exalted are You, [O Allah]; this is a great slander

24:27.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ لَا تَدۡخُلُواْ بُيُوتًا غَيۡرَ بُيُوتِكُمۡ حَتَّىٰ تَسۡتَأۡنِسُواْ وَتُسَلِّمُواْ عَلَىٰٓ أَهۡلِهَاۚ ذَٰلِكُمۡ خَيۡرࣱ لَّكُمۡ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تَذَكَّرُونَ
24:27.en: O you who have believed, do not enter houses other than your own houses until you ascertain welcome and greet their inhabitants. That is best for you; perhaps you will be reminded

24:28.ar: فَإِن لَّمۡ تَجِدُواْ فِيهَآ أَحَدࣰ ا فَلَا تَدۡخُلُوهَا حَتَّىٰ يُؤۡذَنَ لَكُمۡۖ وَإِن قِيلَ لَكُمُ ٱرۡجِعُواْ فَٱرۡجِعُواْۖ هُوَ أَزۡكَىٰ لَكُمۡۚ وَٱللَّهُ بِمَا تَعۡمَلُونَ عَلِيمࣱ‏
24:28.en: And if you do not find anyone therein, do not enter them until permission has been given you. And if it is said to you, "Go back," then go back; it is purer for you. And Allah is Knowing of what you do

24:30.ar: قُل لِّلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ يَغُضُّواْ مِنۡ أَبۡصَٰرِهِمۡ وَيَحۡفَظُواْ فُرُوجَهُمۡۚ ذَٰلِكَ أَزۡكَىٰ لَهُمۡۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ خَبِيرُۢ بِمَا يَصۡنَعُونَ
24:30.en: Tell the believing men to reduce [some] of their vision and guard their private parts. That is purer for them. Indeed, Allah is Acquainted with what they do

24:31.ar: وَقُل لِّلۡمُؤۡمِنَٰتِ يَغۡضُضۡنَ مِنۡ أَبۡصَٰرِهِنَّ وَيَحۡفَظۡنَ فُرُوجَهُنَّ وَلَا يُبۡدِينَ زِينَتَهُنَّ إِلَّا مَا ظَهَرَ مِنۡهَاۖ وَلۡيَضۡرِبۡنَ بِخُمُرِهِنَّ عَلَىٰ جُيُوبِهِنَّۖ وَلَا يُبۡدِينَ زِينَتَهُنَّ إِلَّا لِبُعُولَتِهِنَّ أَوۡ ءَابَآئِهِنَّ أَوۡ ءَابَآءِ بُعُولَتِهِنَّ أَوۡ أَبۡنَآئِهِنَّ أَوۡ أَبۡنَآءِ بُعُولَتِهِنَّ أَوۡ إِخۡوَٰنِهِنَّ أَوۡ بَنِيٓ إِخۡوَٰنِهِنَّ أَوۡ بَنِيٓ أَخَوَٰتِهِنَّ أَوۡ نِسَآئِهِنَّ أَوۡ مَا مَلَكَتۡ أَيۡمَٰنُهُنَّ أَوِ ٱلتَّٰبِعِينَ غَيۡرِ أُوْلِي ٱلۡإِرۡبَةِ مِنَ ٱلرِّجَالِ أَوِ ٱلطِّفۡلِ ٱلَّذِينَ لَمۡ يَظۡهَرُواْ عَلَىٰ عَوۡرَٰتِ ٱلنِّسَآءِۖ وَلَا يَضۡرِبۡنَ بِأَرۡجُلِهِنَّ لِيُعۡلَمَ مَا يُخۡفِينَ مِن زِينَتِهِنَّۚ وَتُوبُوٓاْ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ جَمِيعًا أَيُّهَ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنُونَ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تُفۡلِحُونَ
24:31.en: And tell the believing women to reduce [some] of their vision and guard their private parts and not expose their adornment except that which [necessarily] appears thereof and to wrap [a portion of] their headcovers over their chests and not expose their adornment except to their husbands, their fathers, their husbands' fathers, their sons, their husbands' sons, their brothers, their brothers' sons, their sisters' sons, their women, that which their right hands possess, or those male attendants having no physical desire, or children who are not yet aware of the private aspects of women. And let them not stamp their feet to make known what they conceal of their adornment. And turn to Allah in repentance, all of you, O believers, that you might succeed

24:32.ar: وَأَنكِحُواْ ٱلۡأَيَٰمَىٰ مِنكُمۡ وَٱلصَّٰلِحِينَ مِنۡ عِبَادِكُمۡ وَإِمَآئِكُمۡۚ إِن يَكُونُواْ فُقَرَآءَ يُغۡنِهِمُ ٱللَّهُ مِن فَضۡلِهِۦۗ وَٱللَّهُ وَٰسِعٌ عَلِيمࣱ‏
24:32.en: And marry the unmarried among you and the righteous among your male slaves and female slaves. If they should be poor, Allah will enrich them from His bounty, and Allah is all-Encompassing and Knowing

24:33.ar: وَلۡيَسۡتَعۡفِفِ ٱلَّذِينَ لَا يَجِدُونَ نِكَاحًا حَتَّىٰ يُغۡنِيَهُمُ ٱللَّهُ مِن فَضۡلِهِۦۗ وَٱلَّذِينَ يَبۡتَغُونَ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ مِمَّا مَلَكَتۡ أَيۡمَٰنُكُمۡ فَكَاتِبُوهُمۡ إِنۡ عَلِمۡتُمۡ فِيهِمۡ خَيۡرࣰ اۖ وَءَاتُوهُم مِّن مَّالِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلَّذِيٓ ءَاتَىٰكُمۡۚ وَلَا تُكۡرِهُواْ فَتَيَٰتِكُمۡ عَلَى ٱلۡبِغَآءِ إِنۡ أَرَدۡنَ تَحَصُّنࣰ ا لِّتَبۡتَغُواْ عَرَضَ ٱلۡحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنۡيَاۚ وَمَن يُكۡرِههُّنَّ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ مِنۢ بَعۡدِ إِكۡرَٰهِهِنَّ غَفُورࣱ رَّحِيمࣱ‏
24:33.en: But let them who find not [the means for] marriage abstain [from sexual relations] until Allah enriches them from His bounty. And those who seek a contract [for eventual emancipation] from among whom your right hands possess - then make a contract with them if you know there is within them goodness and give them from the wealth of Allah which He has given you. And do not compel your slave girls to prostitution, if they desire chastity, to seek [thereby] the temporary interests of worldly life. And if someone should compel them, then indeed, Allah is [to them], after their compulsion, Forgiving and Merciful

24:55.ar: وَعَدَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ مِنكُمۡ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ لَيَسۡتَخۡلِفَنَّهُمۡ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ كَمَا ٱسۡتَخۡلَفَ ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبۡلِهِمۡ وَلَيُمَكِّنَنَّ لَهُمۡ دِينَهُمُ ٱلَّذِي ٱرۡتَضَىٰ لَهُمۡ وَلَيُبَدِّلَنَّهُم مِّنۢ بَعۡدِ خَوۡفِهِمۡ أَمۡنࣰ اۚ يَعۡبُدُونَنِي لَا يُشۡرِكُونَ بِي شَيۡـࣰٔ اۚ وَمَن كَفَرَ بَعۡدَ ذَٰلِكَ فَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلۡفَٰسِقُونَ
24:55.en: Allah has promised those who have believed among you and done righteous deeds that He will surely grant them succession [to authority] upon the earth just as He granted it to those before them and that He will surely establish for them [therein] their religion which He has preferred for them and that He will surely substitute for them, after their fear, security, [for] they worship Me, not associating anything with Me. But whoever disbelieves after that - then those are the defiantly disobedient

24:58.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ لِيَسۡتَـٔۡذِنكُمُ ٱلَّذِينَ مَلَكَتۡ أَيۡمَٰنُكُمۡ وَٱلَّذِينَ لَمۡ يَبۡلُغُواْ ٱلۡحُلُمَ مِنكُمۡ ثَلَٰثَ مَرَّٰتࣲۚ مِّن قَبۡلِ صَلَوٰةِ ٱلۡفَجۡرِ وَحِينَ تَضَعُونَ ثِيَابَكُم مِّنَ ٱلظَّهِيرَةِ وَمِنۢ بَعۡدِ صَلَوٰةِ ٱلۡعِشَآءِۚ ثَلَٰثُ عَوۡرَٰتࣲ لَّكُمۡۚ لَيۡسَ عَلَيۡكُمۡ وَلَا عَلَيۡهِمۡ جُنَاحُۢ بَعۡدَهُنَّۚ طَوَّٰفُونَ عَلَيۡكُم بَعۡضُكُمۡ عَلَىٰ بَعۡضࣲۚ كَذَٰلِكَ يُبَيِّنُ ٱللَّهُ لَكُمُ ٱلۡأٓيَٰتِۗ وَٱللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ حَكِيمࣱ‏
24:58.en: O you who have believed, let those whom your right hands possess and those who have not [yet] reached puberty among you ask permission of you [before entering] at three times: before the dawn prayer and when you put aside your clothing [for rest] at noon and after the night prayer. [These are] three times of privacy for you. There is no blame upon you nor upon them beyond these [periods], for they continually circulate among you - some of you, among others. Thus does Allah make clear to you the verses; and Allah is Knowing and Wise

24:59.ar: وَإِذَا بَلَغَ ٱلۡأَطۡفَٰلُ مِنكُمُ ٱلۡحُلُمَ فَلۡيَسۡتَـٔۡذِنُواْ كَمَا ٱسۡتَـٔۡذَنَ ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبۡلِهِمۡۚ كَذَٰلِكَ يُبَيِّنُ ٱللَّهُ لَكُمۡ ءَايَٰتِهِۦۗ وَٱللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ حَكِيمࣱ‏
24:59.en: And when the children among you reach puberty, let them ask permission [at all times] as those before them have done. Thus does Allah make clear to you His verses; and Allah is Knowing and Wise

24:62.ar: إِنَّمَا ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنُونَ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ بِٱللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِۦ وَإِذَا كَانُواْ مَعَهُۥ عَلَىٰٓ أَمۡرࣲ جَامِعࣲ لَّمۡ يَذۡهَبُواْ حَتَّىٰ يَسۡتَـٔۡذِنُوهُۚ إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَسۡتَـٔۡذِنُونَكَ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ يُؤۡمِنُونَ بِٱللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِۦۚ فَإِذَا ٱسۡتَـٔۡذَنُوكَ لِبَعۡضِ شَأۡنِهِمۡ فَأۡذَن لِّمَن شِئۡتَ مِنۡهُمۡ وَٱسۡتَغۡفِرۡ لَهُمُ ٱللَّهَۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورࣱ رَّحِيمࣱ‏
24:62.en: The believers are only those who believe in Allah and His Messenger and, when they are [meeting] with him for a matter of common interest, do not depart until they have asked his permission. Indeed, those who ask your permission, [O Muhammad] - those are the ones who believe in Allah and His Messenger. So when they ask your permission for something of their affairs, then give permission to whom you will among them and ask forgiveness for them of Allah. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful

49:12.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ ٱجۡتَنِبُواْ كَثِيرࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱلظَّنِّ إِنَّ بَعۡضَ ٱلظَّنِّ إِثۡمࣱۖ وَلَا تَجَسَّسُواْ وَلَا يَغۡتَب بَّعۡضُكُم بَعۡضًاۚ أَيُحِبُّ أَحَدُكُمۡ أَن يَأۡكُلَ لَحۡمَ أَخِيهِ مَيۡتࣰ ا فَكَرِهۡتُمُوهُۚ وَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ تَوَّابࣱ رَّحِيمࣱ‏
49:12.en: O you who have believed, avoid much [negative] assumption. Indeed, some assumption is sin. And do not spy or backbite each other. Would one of you like to eat the flesh of his brother when dead? You would detest it. And fear Allah; indeed, Allah is Accepting of repentance and Merciful

49:10.ar: إِنَّمَا ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنُونَ إِخۡوَةࣱ فَأَصۡلِحُواْ بَيۡنَ أَخَوَيۡكُمۡۚ وَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تُرۡحَمُونَ
49:10.en: The believers are but brothers, so make settlement between your brothers. And fear Allah that you may receive mercy

49:13.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ إِنَّا خَلَقۡنَٰكُم مِّن ذَكَرࣲ وَأُنثَىٰ وَجَعَلۡنَٰكُمۡ شُعُوبࣰ ا وَقَبَآئِلَ لِتَعَارَفُوٓاْۚ إِنَّ أَكۡرَمَكُمۡ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ أَتۡقَىٰكُمۡۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلِيمٌ خَبِيرࣱ‏
49:13.en: O mankind, indeed We have created you from male and female and made you peoples and tribes that you may know one another. Indeed, the most noble of you in the sight of Allah is the most righteous of you. Indeed, Allah is Knowing and Acquainted

49:11.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ لَا يَسۡخَرۡ قَوۡمࣱ مِّن قَوۡمٍ عَسَىٰٓ أَن يَكُونُواْ خَيۡرࣰ ا مِّنۡهُمۡ وَلَا نِسَآءࣱ مِّن نِّسَآءٍ عَسَىٰٓ أَن يَكُنَّ خَيۡرࣰ ا مِّنۡهُنَّۖ وَلَا تَلۡمِزُوٓاْ أَنفُسَكُمۡ وَلَا تَنَابَزُواْ بِٱلۡأَلۡقَٰبِۖ بِئۡسَ ٱلِٱسۡمُ ٱلۡفُسُوقُ بَعۡدَ ٱلۡإِيمَٰنِۚ وَمَن لَّمۡ يَتُبۡ فَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلظَّٰلِمُونَ
49:11.en: O you who have believed, let not a people ridicule [another] people; perhaps they may be better than them; nor let women ridicule [other] women; perhaps they may be better than them. And do not insult one another and do not call each other by [offensive] nicknames. Wretched is the name of disobedience after [one's] faith. And whoever does not repent - then it is those who are the wrongdoers

4:11.ar: يُوصِيكُمُ ٱللَّهُ فِيٓ أَوۡلَٰدِكُمۡۖ لِلذَّكَرِ مِثۡلُ حَظِّ ٱلۡأُنثَيَيۡنِۚ فَإِن كُنَّ نِسَآءࣰ فَوۡقَ ٱثۡنَتَيۡنِ فَلَهُنَّ ثُلُثَا مَا تَرَكَۖ وَإِن كَانَتۡ وَٰحِدَةࣰ فَلَهَا ٱلنِّصۡفُۚ وَلِأَبَوَيۡهِ لِكُلِّ وَٰحِدࣲ مِّنۡهُمَا ٱلسُّدُسُ مِمَّا تَرَكَ إِن كَانَ لَهُۥ وَلَدࣱۚ فَإِن لَّمۡ يَكُن لَّهُۥ وَلَدࣱ وَوَرِثَهُۥٓ أَبَوَاهُ فَلِأُمِّهِ ٱلثُّلُثُۚ فَإِن كَانَ لَهُۥٓ إِخۡوَةࣱ فَلِأُمِّهِ ٱلسُّدُسُۚ مِنۢ بَعۡدِ وَصِيَّةࣲ يُوصِي بِهَآ أَوۡ دَيۡنٍۗ ءَابَآؤُكُمۡ وَأَبۡنَآؤُكُمۡ لَا تَدۡرُونَ أَيُّهُمۡ أَقۡرَبُ لَكُمۡ نَفۡعࣰ اۚ فَرِيضَةࣰ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِۗ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ عَلِيمًا حَكِيمࣰ ا
4:11.en: Allah instructs you concerning your children: for the male, what is equal to the share of two females. But if there are [only] daughters, two or more, for them is two thirds of one's estate. And if there is only one, for her is half. And for one's parents, to each one of them is a sixth of his estate if he left children. But if he had no children and the parents [alone] inherit from him, then for his mother is one third. And if he had brothers [or sisters], for his mother is a sixth, after any bequest he [may have] made or debt. Your parents or your children - you know not which of them are nearest to you in benefit. [These shares are] an obligation [imposed] by Allah. Indeed, Allah is ever Knowing and Wise

4:75.ar: وَمَا لَكُمۡ لَا تُقَٰتِلُونَ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ وَٱلۡمُسۡتَضۡعَفِينَ مِنَ ٱلرِّجَالِ وَٱلنِّسَآءِ وَٱلۡوِلۡدَٰنِ ٱلَّذِينَ يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنَآ أَخۡرِجۡنَا مِنۡ هَٰذِهِ ٱلۡقَرۡيَةِ ٱلظَّالِمِ أَهۡلُهَا وَٱجۡعَل لَّنَا مِن لَّدُنكَ وَلِيࣰّ ا وَٱجۡعَل لَّنَا مِن لَّدُنكَ نَصِيرًا
4:75.en: And what is [the matter] with you that you fight not in the cause of Allah and [for] the oppressed among men, women, and children who say, "Our Lord, take us out of this city of oppressive people and appoint for us from Yourself a protector and appoint for us from Yourself a helper

wzXw7BCVRs0.title: Seerah Halaqah: Social Rulings of Years Five and Six (Part 1)
wzXw7BCVRs0.one_line: Rulings revealed after the slander of Aishah in An-Nur and Al-Hujurat on gossip, privacy, modesty and respect, leading into the story of Banu Ubayriq.
wzXw7BCVRs0.summary: Continuing from the slander against Aishah, the sheikh draws out the lesson that a Muslim must refuse outright to take part in gossip, especially about someone's chastity, and walk away if it continues. He explains that Allah raised the early community by addressing real problems as they happened, and asks whether we will make the same decision today. He reviews the rulings of Surat An-Nur: seeking permission before entering homes, lowering the gaze for men and women, making marriage easy even for the poor, and children asking permission at three times of day. In the middle of these rules comes the promise of stewardship, safety and security for believers, which he says is reached through these everyday manners, beginning in the home. He moves to Surat Al-Hujurat: avoid bad assumptions about people, read words in the best light, reconcile quarrelling brothers, reject racism because only piety matters to Allah, and never mock or insult. He makes an exception for parents, whose job is to be watchful, and thanks his own strict father. He also covers inheritance rights for women and care for the weak, then introduces the story of a theft in Medina involving the sons of Ubayriq, Qatadah ibn al-Nu'man and his uncle.

outline.heading: Refuse to take part in gossip
outline.gist: When people speak about someone's chastity, the believer says it is not proper for us to speak of this.

outline.heading: Hard but essential; Allah teaches through real events
outline.gist: Walking away is difficult but central; the Quran raised the community by addressing problems as they occurred.

outline.heading: The choice before us today
outline.gist: Each of us must decide whether we will spread, entertain or refuse gossip.

outline.heading: Asking permission before entering homes
outline.gist: Respect privacy: do not enter or look into a house until permitted.

outline.heading: Lowering the gaze and making marriage easy
outline.gist: Both men and women are told to lower their gaze and guard chastity; society should help even poor people marry.

outline.heading: The promise of stewardship in An-Nur
outline.gist: A unique promise sits among the rules: believers will be granted authority, a firm religion and security.

outline.heading: Stewardship is earned through these rules
outline.gist: What Muslims hope for comes through adhering to these everyday commands.

outline.heading: Children asking permission at three times
outline.gist: Teaching children to knock at set times is where building a society begins.

outline.heading: Leaving a gathering with permission; respecting others
outline.gist: Believers do not walk out of a group without permission; be mindful and respectful of everyone around you.

outline.heading: Avoid bad assumptions
outline.gist: Suspicion does no good, fills the heart with bad feelings and harms brotherhood.

outline.heading: Parents are the exception
outline.gist: Parents are meant to be watchful; he thanks his strict father and warns that neglected children suffer.

outline.heading: Take words in the best way
outline.gist: If something can be read well or badly, read it well and move on; suspicion wastes time and energy.

outline.heading: Reconciliation and equality
outline.gist: Believers are brothers who must make peace between each other; colour, wealth and origin mean nothing to Allah.

outline.heading: Only piety matters
outline.gist: We all return to dust; what remains is goodness and purity of heart.

outline.heading: No mockery or name-calling
outline.gist: The one you mock may be better than you; respect governs entering, leaving and visiting.

outline.heading: Inheritance rights for women
outline.gist: Before these verses women inherited nothing and were even inherited; brothers today must not pressure sisters to give up their share.

outline.heading: Standing up for the weak
outline.gist: The Quran repeatedly demands care for those who cannot defend themselves.

outline.heading: Will we adopt these values?
outline.gist: Societies change when a generation holds to values the previous one neglected.

outline.heading: The theft story: the sons of Ubayriq and Qatadah's uncle
outline.gist: He introduces the players: troublesome brothers, the devout Qatadah ibn al-Nu'man, and his newly Muslim uncle.

quran.point: Believers should have said it is not right for us to speak of this.
Do not enter houses without permission.
Men and women lower their gaze and guard their chastity.
Marry off the single; if poor Allah will enrich them; those who cannot should stay chaste.
Allah's promise of stewardship, a firm religion and security for believers.
Children ask permission at three times of privacy.
Once they reach puberty they ask permission at all times.
True believers do not leave a collective matter without permission.
Avoid much suspicion; some suspicion is sin.
Believers are brothers; make peace between them.
The most honoured is the most pious, regardless of origin.
Do not mock others; they may be better than you; no insulting nicknames.
Inheritance shares given to women for the first time.
Standing up for the oppressed and weak who have no helper.

hadith.gist: A companion said that even if he saw a brother with alcohol dripping from his beard he would assume someone had spilled it on him.

takeaways: Refuse to listen to gossip about people's honour and walk away if it continues
Knock and ask permission before entering, and teach children to do the same
